hold_text: Tier-2 by path: this adds a new route to src/web/api/routers/diag.py and a new accessor to src/units/accounts/clients.py, and src/** is in this guard's own TIER2_PATHS. It needs one operator OK before merge, and merging it restarts ict-web-api. WHAT THE OPERATOR IS ACTUALLY APPROVING, stated so the read is short: a READ-ONLY diag route and the accessor behind it. It grades nothing, re-arms nothing, opens no order path, cannot refuse a trade, and returns no credential material. It is ADDITIVE — the new accessor has exactly one caller (the new route), so no existing reader, sweep, reconciler or order path changes behaviour by a single line; account_open_positions and account_bybit_open_orders are untouched. The one non-obvious cost is broker calls: the route issues 1 + N get_positions reads per Bybit account (the settleCoin page plus one per configured symbol, N=4 on bybit_2) but ONLY when a human calls the endpoint — it is on no tick, no timer and no sweep, so it adds zero to the trader loop and cannot reach the June 2026 wedge class. WHY IT IS WORTH A TIER-2 APPROVAL AT ALL: every Bybit position reader in the repo reduces the venue's answer identically (skip size<=0, dedupe by SYMBOL), so 'the venue is genuinely flat', 'the venue returned a ZERO-SIZE hedge sibling book' and 'the venue returned no row at all' are ONE observation to every consumer. That collapse blocked root-cause on TWO real-money P1 investigations one day apart — BL-20260908-BYBIT-POSITION-PROTECTION-GRADES-A-SYMBOL-OFF-ROWS0-SO-A-HEDGE-BOOK-READS-FLAT-AND-A-LIVE-POSITION-IS-CLOSED states it verbatim, and MI-221 hit the identical wall on a different function. Until this lands, MI-221's central question — does the VENUE not return the bybit_2 ETHUSDT position, or does the BOT drop it after the read? — cannot be answered by anyone, and STEP 2 (the fix) cannot be scoped because its scope depends on that answer. NOT IN THIS DIFF, deliberately: the STEP 3 detector (a venue-anchored residual sweep that would give the safety sweeps a third anchor) is PROPOSED in docs/claude/work/BYBIT2-ETH-PHANTOM-CLOSE-2026-09-09.md and NOT implemented — it changes what the reconciler adopts, which is a separate and larger Tier-2 decision that should not ride an instrument PR. No order was placed, modified or cancelled on bybit_2 in this session; every venue read was a GET.
why: MI-221, under the operator directive of 2026-09-09 ('the bot needs to fix this ... the system cannot and will not rely on me manually checking and fixing every trade'). Ships STEP 1 only: the discriminating instrument. GET /api/diag/bybit_raw_positions returns the raw Bybit get_positions payload un-deduped, un-filtered, zero-size rows included, every row carrying position_idx and both size_raw and size. It runs the settleCoin page AND a symbol-scoped read for EVERY configured symbol — including symbols the page already returned — because the disagreement between the two views is itself the finding (BL-20260713-BYBIT2-BTC-SETTLECOIN-BLIND), and a `sym in seen` skip would hide exactly the case it was built to see. size is carried twice because _f-style coercion turns an unparseable size into 0.0, manufacturing the flat reading the route exists to distinguish. Per-query query_state is three-way and never collapsed (rows_returned / no_rows — the venue answered EMPTY, a real positive measurement / could_not_look — the call raised, which says nothing about the world) with row_count null rather than 0 on the last, and one failing symbol query never sinks the others. Symbols resolve through _bybit_configured_symbols rather than the bare account['symbols'] its sibling reads, so a hand-built reduced cfg cannot silently yield an empty cross-check. ALSO IN THIS DIFF: the mandatory docs/api-tier-policy.md row, a bot-api-reference row, 8 tests, and an addendum to the MI-221 evidence doc that WITHDRAWS that doc's earlier framing — it routed the remedy to the operator, which the directive above rules out. The addendum records the class finding, verified in code this session rather than inherited: every protective sweep anchors on one of exactly two lists — the VENUE list (account_open_positions at order_monitor.py:3128) or the JOURNAL-OPEN list (SELECT ... FROM trades WHERE status='open' at order_monitor.py:9845) — and trade 5471 is in NEITHER, which is why nothing saw it. The repair chain itself is already built, unconditional and venue-correct (_attempt_naked_autoprotect:7706 -> set_trading_stop Full mode, hedge-aware, no enable gate), so the missing piece is a third anchor, not a repair. TESTING CAVEAT, stated rather than implied: pytest is not installed in this sandbox, so the 8 new tests were NOT run here; the accessor was exercised directly instead and 4 properties pass, including the exact MI-221 shape (a flat sibling book listed FIRST and the live book second — both survive, where symbol dedupe keeps only the first). run_guards.py --base main gave PASS 67 / FAIL 5; the single failure this change caused (check_backlog_refs, a truncated backlog id in the route docstring) is fixed and re-verified green, and the remaining four are environmental here — pytest absent (2), lint-imports absent (exit 127), and pr-landing-guard, which this file answers.
